behavior_constraints: forge build detects dependency cycles and exits with a non-zero status instead of looping forever, printing an error message that names every package in the cycle.

A package cache is invalidated when any transitive dependency has a newer last-build timestamp than the package's own last build, so rebuilding an upstream library triggers rebuilds of downstream packages.
FORGE_CFLAGS and FORGE_LIBS for every package include include and library paths for the full transitive dependency closure, not only direct dependencies.

forge artifact pack <name> includes build/deps.manifest inside the packaged build directory; after extraction it is available at build/deps.manifest and contains one <dep_name>=<dep_version> line per direct dependency, with an empty file for packages with no direct dependencies.
forge report displays every package name in full with proper column alignment and no truncation at 12 characters.

forge config generate ENV resolves nested variable references such as ${REGION_${ENV}} iteratively until no unresolved references remain or a maximum depth is reached, while still performing simple ${VAR} substitution.

parse_manifest joins values ending with a trailing backslash to the following line, strips the trailing backslash and leading whitespace on the continuation line, and no longer keeps the backslash verbatim or ignores continuation lines.
tests/run_tests.sh has no TODO markers, fills every TODO test case, adds coverage for all seven fixed behaviors including edge cases, and passes.
entities.summary: Round 1 demands stabilization of forgekit by adding dependency cycle detection, transitive cache invalidation, transitive compiler/linker path injection, artifact dependency manifests, full-name build reports, nested config variable resolution, manifest backslash continuation handling, and complete test coverage.

instruction_head: `/app` contains `forgekit`, our internal bash-based build orchestrator for a monorepo of eight C packages -- four libraries (`libbase`, `libcrypto`, `libnet`, `libstore`) and four services (`svc-auth`, `svc-gateway`, `svc-worker`, `svc-scheduler`). The `./forge` CLI handles dependency resolution, build ordering, caching, artifact packaging, deployment config generation from templates, and build reporting. Package metadata lives in `package.forge` manifest files using a section-based key-value fo

behavior_constraints: forge build --all accepts optional -j N (N>=1); when -j is omitted it is sequential equivalent to -j 1.
Parallel builds respect dependency ordering: a package may start only after all dependencies complete, and at most N packages build concurrently.
forge build --package NAME -j N builds the package and its dependency chain using parallelism while preserving dependency order.
Each package's parallel build output is buffered and printed together under an '=== [PKG] ===' header after it finishes; output from different packages must never interleave.

If a package fails during parallel build, concurrently running packages continue to completion, no further eligible packages start, exit status is non-zero, and the error message lists every failed package as 'Build failed for: PKG1, PKG2'.
build, test, clean, and artifact pack accept --profile debug|release; default is release when omitted.
setup_build_env accepts an optional profile argument as setup_build_env PKG PROFILE.
FORGE_CFLAGS includes debug flags '-g -O0 -DDEBUG' or release flags '-O2 -DNDEBUG -s' plus dependency include paths for the selected profile.
Each profile builds into packages/{pkg}/build/{profile}/ by setting BUILD_DIR=build/{profile}.
Cache stamps are namespaced by profile as {pkg}-{profile}.stamp; building one profile must not invalidate or satisfy another profile's cache.

lib/cache.sh: init_cache/is_cache_valid/update_cache/invalidate_cache/clean_cache must become profile-namespaced and profile-scoped

entities.summary: This round demands parallel build execution with buffered output and failure aggregation, debug/release build profiles across build/test/clean/artifact, and a DOT dependency graph export with reverse-dependency subgraph support.

instruction_head:
# Round 2: Parallel Build Pipeline, Build Profiles & Graph Export

ForgeKit currently builds every package sequentially. With eight packages and growing, full rebuilds are slow. The team wants parallel builds, the ability to target different build profiles, and a way to visualize the dependency graph.

## 1. Parallel Build Execution

`forge build --all` must accept an optional **`-j N`** flag (where `N >= 1`) to build independent packages concurrently. When `-j` is omitted, the default is sequen

behavior_constraints: get_src_mtime must include the modification time of package.forge when computing source freshness
Any change to package.forge (version, deps, build command) must trigger a rebuild on next build
clean_package must accept an optional profile parameter; when given, only remove build/<profile>/ leaving other profiles intact
clean_package without a profile must continue removing the entire build/ directory (existing behavior)
forge clean --all --profile PROF must only invalidate cache stamps for that profile, not all stamps
forge clean --all without --profile continues to remove all cache stamps (existing behavior)
forge clean --package NAME must invalidate that package's cache stamp(s) after removing build artifacts
forge clean --package NAME --profile PROF must invalidate only that profile's stamp for the package
forge clean --package NAME without --profile must invalidate all profile stamps for that package
Existing behavior of forge build --all, parallel builds, DOT graph export, and artifact packing must be preserved

instruction_head:
# Round 3: Build Cache & Clean Correctness Fixes

The team has filed three bug reports against the build cache and clean subsystems. Each bug causes stale builds or unintended data loss. All three must be fixed.

## Bug 1: Manifest Changes Don't Trigger Rebuilds

**Steps to reproduce:**
```bash
forge build --all                          # builds everything
# Edit packages/libbase/package.forge (e.g., change version from 1.0.0 to 1.0.1)
forge build --all                          # expected: rebui

behavior_constraints: `forge build --changed` rebuilds only packages with invalid cache plus their transitive reverse dependents, in dependency order
When nothing changed, `forge build --changed` prints 'Everything up to date.' and exits 0
Skipped packages under `--changed` produce no build output
Every rebuilt package (including reverse-dependents with unchanged source) regenerates its build artifact so mtime advances
`--changed` composes with `--profile` and `-j` flags
`forge impact PACKAGE` prints the queried package first, then transitive reverse dependents in topological order (dependencies before dependents), one per line
`forge impact svc-auth` prints only `svc-auth`
`forge deps --why PKG1 PKG2` prints the shortest dependency path from PKG1 to PKG2 using ` -> ` separators
If no path exists, `forge deps --why PKG1 PKG2` prints 'No dependency path from PKG1 to PKG2.'
If PKG1 equals PKG2, `forge deps --why PKG1 PKG2` prints the single package name and exits 0
entities.summary: This round adds selective rebuild based on cache validity and reverse dependencies, impact analysis listing transitive reverse dependents, and a shortest dependency-path query command.

instruction_head:
# Round 4: Selective Rebuild and Impact Analysis

Full rebuilds are wasteful when only one package changed. We need a way to rebuild only what's actually affected by a change, and a way to query which packages would be impacted before committing to a rebuild.

## 1. Selective Rebuild

Add `forge build --changed` (works with `-j N` and `--profile`). This command:

1. Identifies every package whose source files, Makefile, or manifest have changed since its last successful build (i.e., cache is inv

behavior_constraints: Source hash for a package is SHA256 of newline-separated sorted SHA256 hashes of all files under src/ plus the Makefile plus package.forge
touch-ing a file without changing its content does NOT invalidate the cache because the SHA256 is unchanged
Cache is valid only when the package's current source hash matches the stored hash AND every transitive dependency's current source hash matches the hash recorded at last build time
Cache stamp file is .forge_cache/<pkg>-<profile>.hash with format: own hash on line 1, then <dep_name>:<dep_hash> lines for each transitive dependency
Old .stamp files from the timestamp-based cache are treated as cache misses without error
When a package is rebuilt the old .stamp file (if any) is replaced by the new .hash file
forge cache status prints a table with columns PACKAGE, PROFILE, STATUS
forge cache status --package NAME shows status for only that package
STATUS field values are: cached (<first 8 chars of hash>...), stale (src changed), stale (dep NAME changed), no cache
forge cache status --profile defaults to release

lib/builder.sh build_package and build_changed_packages which invoke cache validity checks
lib/common.sh clean_package which calls cache invalidation and must handle .hash stamps
Round 3 profile-aware cache invalidation (stamp file naming changes from .stamp to .hash)

entities.summary: Replace the timestamp-based build cache with a content-addressable SHA256 cache that stores per-package source hashes plus transitive dependency hashes, add a forge cache status command, and treat old .stamp files as cache misses.

instruction_head:
# Round 5: Content-Addressable Build Cache

The timestamp-based cache has a fundamental flaw: operations like `touch` that modify mtime without changing content cause unnecessary rebuilds. We're switching to content-addressable caching based on SHA256 hashes.

## Cache Key Computation

Replace the timestamp-based freshness check with a content hash. The cache key for a package is computed as:

```
SHA256(sorted concatenation of SHA256 hashes of all files in src/ + Makefile + package.forge)
```

behavior_constraints: Every forge build invocation appends JSON events to .forge_journal/events.jsonl, one JSON object per line, append-only
Each event contains exactly: timestamp, event, package, profile, duration_ms, cache_hit, trigger
timestamp is ISO 8601 from `date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ`
event is one of build_start, build_complete, build_fail, build_skip
For cache-valid packages, emit a single build_skip event with duration_ms=0, cache_hit=true, trigger=manual
For cache-invalid packages, emit build_start first (duration_ms=0, cache_hit=false), then build_complete or build_fail with duration_ms measuring actual build time
trigger for actual builds follows priority order: no_cache (no entry), source_changed (own source changed), dep_changed (dependency changed), manual (explicit rebuild not otherwise stale)
forge journal displays recent events with columns: timestamp, event type, package (left-padded to 16 chars), profile, detail (duration_ms+'ms' or 'cached')
forge journal defaults to 50 most recent events
forge journal --last N shows only N most recent events
entities.summary: This round demands a structured append-only JSONL build event journal with timing, cache-hit, and trigger fields emitted around each build action, a forge journal query/clear command with filtering options, parallel-safe appending via flock, and a Last Build duration column in forge report.

instruction_head:
# Round 6: Build Event Journal and Timing

We need observability into the build process. Add a structured event journal that records every build action with timing information.

## Event Journal

Every `forge build` invocation writes JSON events to `.forge_journal/events.jsonl` (one JSON object per line, append-only). Each event has the following fields:

```json
{
  "timestamp": "2024-01-15T10:30:45Z",
  "event": "build_start|build_complete|build_skip|build_fail",
  "package": "libbase",
  "pro

behavior_constraints: Source hash computation must include the selected build profile name as an additional input to the SHA256 hash
get_src_hash PACKAGE [PROFILE] must be supported by the cache helper API and default to the existing default profile when PROFILE is omitted
Profile-specific cache stamps must never be compared against a profile-agnostic content hash; switching profiles forces rehash/rebuild
All journal appends must acquire an exclusive flock on .forge_journal/.lock, write the JSON line, then release the lock
Journal writes must be correct and lossless under -j 4 parallelism (no interleaved or dropped events)
forge journal | wc -l after a parallel --all build with -j 4 must yield at least 2 events per built package (start+complete)
When updating a package cache stamp after a successful build, record the CURRENT source hashes of all transitive dependencies (post-rebuild state), not the pre-build hashes
Cache stamp update for a dependent must occur only after its dependencies have been rebuilt and their stamps updated
After forge build --changed rebuilds a changed package and its dependents, forge cache status must report all rebuilt packages as cached (not stale)
Existing behavior for non-parallel, single-profile, and unchanged-source cases must be preserved
entities.summary: Fix content-hash cache to be profile-aware in source hash computation, serialize journal appends with flock under parallel builds, and ensure --changed rebuilds record current transitive dependency hashes in cache stamps so dependents are not reported stale.

behavior_constraints: Manifest `[targets]` section maps target name to a script path relative to package directory.
Manifest `[hooks]` section defines pre_build, post_build, pre_test, post_test hook scripts.
`forge run TARGET --all` runs the target for every package that defines it in dependency order; packages without the target are silently skipped.
`forge run TARGET --package NAME` runs the target for that package after ensuring dependencies' targets have run.
Target and hook scripts execute in the package directory with FORGE_ROOT, FORGE_CFLAGS, FORGE_LDFLAGS, FORGE_LIBS, FORGE_PROFILE environment variables set.
A target script that exits non-zero marks the package as failed and yields a non-zero overall exit status.
Per-package output is labeled with `=== [pkg:target] ===` before the script's stdout/stderr.
pre_build runs before build; non-zero aborts the build for that package and is treated as a build failure.
post_build runs after a successful build; non-zero logs a warning but build is still considered successful.
pre_test and post_test run around the test step with the same semantics as the build hooks.

instruction_head:
# Round 8: Build Targets and Pre/Post Hooks

ForgeKit needs a way to run custom per-package commands beyond just `build` and `test`. Add support for named build targets and lifecycle hooks.

```ini

lint = scripts/lint.sh
format = scripts/format.sh
docs = scripts/generate_docs.sh
```
